courier-relay/cross-account-delivery-ide:
Courier Relay: delivery identity and acceptance-rule contract across protocol versions (identity established for trial-ewy on protocol "1"; acceptance rule revised for trial-tfh with permanent adoption of protocol "2" as current; "accepted" command added for trial-tau on protocol "2" only; "accepted" extended for trial-hjc to also support explicit protocol "1").

Identity (unchanged by protocol version):
- Protocol "1" identity (used by "count" and by "accepted" when protocol "1" is explicit): delivery_id ALONE identifies a delivery across all accounts -- the same delivery_id under a different account_id is still the SAME delivery, per the providers original delivery-ID allocation guarantee (vendor/protocol-1.md). This is the original provider contract that shipped with the initial "count" issue (trial-adg).
- Protocol "2" identity (used by "summary", and by "accepted" for protocol "2"/omitted): the pair (account_id, delivery_id) identifies a delivery -- the same delivery_id under a different account_id is a SEPARATE delivery. This is the newer contract from trial-tfh/trial-ewy.
- The single-account "count" command is unaffected by this distinction in practice since it only ever sees one accounts receipts; its delivery_id-alone dedupe is a code-simplicity choice for count, not evidence against the protocol-1 cross-account identity rule.

Acceptance rule, protocol "1" (still explicitly supported, no longer current): within one identity group, the accepted receipt is the one with the EARLIEST occurred_at (compared as a UTC instant); ties broken by the lexicographically (Unicode code-point) smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates.

Acceptance rule, protocol "2" (current as of trial-tfh; provider permanently adopted this contract, approved by the integration owner): within one identity group, the accepted receipt is the one with the LATEST occurred_at (UTC instant); ties still broken by smallest record_id. All other receipts in the group are duplicates.

Protocol selection: an omitted "protocol" field selects the current protocol (now "2"). Explicit "protocol":"1" or "protocol":"2" selects that versions rule set for "count" and "summary"; both remain supported. accepted_count = number of distinct identity-group keys present; duplicate_count = total receipts - accepted_count. Empty batch -> 0/0.

"accepted" command (added trial-tau for protocol "2" only; extended trial-hjc to add protocol "1"): ACCEPTED_SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS is now {"1","2"} (previously {"2"} only) -- an explicit "protocol":"1" request is accepted, not {"error":"unknown_command"}. The command selects its identity key function AND its earliest/latest-wins rule together based on the requested protocol: protocol "1" uses the protocol-1 identity (delivery_id alone) with earliest-wins/smallest-record_id-tie-break, using the ORIGINAL provider contract from vendor/protocol-1.md (same contract "count" protocol "1" uses); protocol "2"/omitted uses the (account_id, delivery_id) identity with latest-wins, as before. Response shape is unchanged: exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, receipts. The receipts array holds the accepted representative from each group, fields/payload/timestamp spelling unchanged, in ORIGINAL INPUT ORDER (not group order) -- achieved by filtering the original input list to the winning record_ids. accepted_count/duplicate_count for protocol "1" match "count" for an equivalent single-account request, and for protocol "2" match "summary" for an equivalent request. Empty input -> receipts [] and both counts zero; a single input receipt is always returned unchanged as the sole accepted representative, regardless of protocol.

Basis: trial-adg issue description and vendor/protocol-1.md (protocol 1 original contract: delivery_id-alone identity, earliest-wins, smallest-record_id tie-break), trial-ewy issue description (protocol 2 identity contract), trial-tfh issue description (protocol 2 permanent adoption, integration-owner approval), trial-tau issue description (accepted command contract, original protocol-2-only scope, response shape, original-input-order requirement), and trial-hjc issue description (extending accepted to explicit protocol "1" using the original provider contract, same response shape, same original-input-order preservation). Implemented in main.py via a shared dedupe(receipts, key_fn, protocol) helper (latest_wins = protocol == "2") returning the winning (instant, record_id) per key; count/summary derive counts from it, and accepted() selects key_fn per protocol (delivery_id alone for "1", (account_id, delivery_id) for "2"/omitted) then filters the original receipts list by winning record_id to build the ordered receipts array. Verified via public test suites accepted_1 (new, protocol 1: empty and single-receipt cases) and accepted_2, plus a manual cross-account-same-delivery_id check confirming protocol "1" dedupes D-1 across accounts A and B while protocol "2" would keep them separate.
